title: Optical character recognition (OCR): which images does Microsoft 365 read for sensitive text, and what does it cost?
summary: The documented scanning behaviour, billing rules, limits and separate eDiscovery settings are supported by Microsoft Learn. Two control paths reach the right place but stop before the final scope or estimation controls.

claims.claim: OCR extracts text inside images for Microsoft 365 to process.
claims.quote: The optical character recognition (OCR) service in SharePoint lets you extract printed or handwritten text from images and documents.

claims.claim: Purview OCR is an optional feature enabled at tenant level.
claims.quote: OCR scanning is an optional feature that you must enable at the tenant level.

claims.where: What it is; Four things called OCR
claims.claim: Configured Purview OCR lets existing DLP policies scan image text.
claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.where: What it is; Four things called OCR
claims.claim: Configured Purview OCR lets existing insider risk management policies use image text.
claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.where: What it is; Four things called OCR
claims.claim: Configured Purview OCR lets existing records management policies use image text.
claims.quote: When you configure the OCR settings, Microsoft Purview applies your existing policies for data loss prevention (DLP), records management, and insider risk management (IRM) to images and text-based content.

claims.claim: The SharePoint OCR service automatically extracts image text from files added to document libraries.
claims.quote: The feature automatically scans the image files, extracts the relevant text, and makes the text from the images available for search and indexing.

claims.where: summary; What it is: Four things called OCR

claims.quote: The extracted information is indexed in search and can be made available for compliance features like data loss prevention (DLP).

claims.quote: The extracted information is indexed in search and can be made available for compliance features like data loss prevention (DLP).

claims.claim: Enabled case OCR processes only files reindexed during Advanced indexing and added to a review set.
claims.quote:
When you turn on this setting, OCR processing runs on image files when they're advanced indexed and added to a review set.
OCR processing only occurs on files that are reindexed during the Advanced indexing process.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Risks and limits: Separate switches
claims.claim: Tenant-level OCR does not enable eDiscovery OCR, which must be enabled per case.
claims.quote:
Enabling tenant-level OCR doesn't enable eDiscovery OCR.
You need to enable OCR functionality for each case that you create in eDiscovery.

claims.where: What it is: Four things called OCR; controls[5].note
claims.claim: Case-level eDiscovery OCR does not incur tenant-level OCR charges.
claims.quote: The case level setting for OCR is distinct from the tenant level OCR setting and doesn't incur the charges associated to that setting.

claims.where: What it is: Four things called OCR, Data Security Investigations row
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations automatically extracts image text during preparation for AI analysis.
claims.quote: OCR text extraction occurs automatically during data preparation and the extracted text is vectorized for use in AI-based analysis tools.

claims.where: What it is: Four things called OCR, Data Security Investigations row
claims.claim: Automatic OCR in Data Security Investigations is not an additional charge.
claims.quote: Extraction of images is part of adding items to an investigation scope and automatic OCR processing isn't an additional charge for your organization.

claims.claim: Communication Compliance has built-in OCR functionality.
claims.quote: Communication Compliance has its own built-in OCR scanning functionality as described in this section

claims.claim: Without OCR, DLP cannot scan image-based content such as an attached photograph.
claims.quote: Without OCR, DLP policies, and auto-labeling policies can't scan image-based content, scanned documents, screenshots, and invoices, leaving sensitive data in images unprotected.

claims.claim: With OCR configured, a credit-card DLP condition scans both text and images in selected locations.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview scans for credit card numbers in both text and images at all of the chosen locations.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing: How Purview counts
claims.claim: Each image scanned by Purview OCR counts as one billable transaction.
claims.quote: Each image scanned counts as one transaction.

claims.quote: After an Azure subscription is linked to pay-as-you-go, OCR will be automatically set up and enabled for all SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: The SharePoint OCR service is on by default for libraries in all SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: By default, the OCR service is turned on for libraries in all SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: SharePoint subsites are not supported by the OCR service.
claims.quote: Subsites aren't supported.

claims.claim: When service and DLP site scopes differ, Microsoft enables the maximum set of sites for OCR.
claims.quote: If there are different sites specified for the service and data loss prevention, the maximum number of sites will be enabled for OCR.

claims.claim: Overlapping SharePoint service and DLP OCR processing is not charged twice.
claims.quote: You won't be charged twice for processing.

claims.claim: After billing is entered, the compliance admin can configure Purview OCR without extra setup or licensing requirements.
claims.quote: After you enter billing information in Microsoft Syntex, your Compliance admin can configure OCR in Microsoft Purview without any extra setup or licensing requirements.

claims.quote: An Azure subscription in the same tenant as the service

claims.quote: An Azure resource group in that subscription

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Four things called OCR
claims.claim: The document processing OCR meter charges $0.001 USD per transaction.
claims.quote: Optical character recognition | The number of pages processed for images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, or BMP); the number of pages processed for PDF, TIF, or TIFF; or the number of embedded images in Teams chats and email messages. Each of these counts as one transaction. | $0.001/transaction

claims.claim: The OCR meter counts image/PDF/TIF/TIFF pages or embedded images in Teams chats and email messages as transactions.
claims.quote: The number of pages processed for images (JPEG, JPG, PNG, or BMP); the number of pages processed for PDF, TIF, or TIFF; or the number of embedded images in Teams chats and email messages. Each of these counts as one transaction.

claims.claim: The document processing price list says OCR processing occurs every time a file is edited.
claims.quote: Processing occurs every time the file is edited.

claims.claim: The Purview OCR page says embedded images are not rescanned when only text is updated.
claims.quote: However, in embedded file types, if only text is updated, images aren't scanned again.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: How Purview counts
claims.claim: Each PDF page is charged separately, making a ten-page PDF ten scans.
claims.quote: For example, if there are 10 pages in a PDF file, an OCR scan of the PDF file counts as 10 separate scans.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: How Purview counts
claims.claim: A scanned image can be reused by any number of DLP, insider risk, auto-labelling and records management policies without extra charge.
claims.quote: Additionally, you can use each scanned image in any number of policies across data loss prevention, insider risk management, auto-labeling, and records management at no extra charge.

claims.claim: Small Exchange images such as logos and signatures are scanned and billed once per unique image tenant-wide over a moving five-day window.
claims.quote: Small images, such as logos and signatures that are sent in email via Microsoft Exchange, are scanned and billed only once per unique image across all users of the tenant for a moving window of five days.

claims.claim: The endpoint OCR cache is maintained for 30 days.
claims.quote: For Endpoint, the cache is maintained for 30 days.

claims.claim: Standalone images in SharePoint and OneDrive have no OCR caching mechanism.
claims.quote: There's no caching mechanism for standalone images in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Only new images

claims.quote: Only images uploaded after OCR is enabled are scanned.

claims.claim: Incoming, internal and outgoing emails are all in OCR scope by default.
claims.quote: By default, incoming email (email from users outside the organization), internal mails (email shared within the users of the organization), and outgoing email (email sent to users outside the organization) are subject to OCR scanning.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Email volume; controls[0].note; What to check
claims.claim: Changing All sender groups to Specific sender groups and specifying internal groups excludes incoming mail and narrows scans.
claims.quote: To exclude incoming mails from OCR scan, change the OCR settings from the default scope of All sender groups to the Specific sender groups and specify the internal groups that you want OCR to scan.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Email volume; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Advanced Setting (Only Exchange) restricts OCR to mail sent outside the organisation.
claims.quote: To restrict OCR scans to mails sent outside the organization only, select the option under Advanced Setting (Only Exchange). After selecting this checkbox, neither incoming mails nor any internal communications are OCRed.

claims.claim: DLP policy tips are not supported for images in Exchange.
claims.quote: Data loss prevention policy tips aren't supported for images in Exchange.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risks and limits: Device bandwidth
claims.claim: Windows and macOS OCR's default bandwidth limit is 1,024 MB per device per day.
claims.quote: When OCR is turned on for Windows and macOS devices, the devices start sending messages to the cloud for scanning. The default bandwidth limit is 1,024 MB of data per device per day.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Device bandwidth; What to check
claims.claim: OCR stops at the daily bandwidth limit, which can be increased to continue scanning.
claims.quote: OCR stops scanning images once this daily limit is reached. If you want to continue scanning images, you can increase the bandwidth limit.

claims.claim: The endpoint classification bandwidth limit applies per device over a rolling 24-hour period.
claims.quote: set a limit on how much bandwidth can be used in a rolling 24-hour period. You configure the limit in Endpoint DLP settings and it applies per device.

claims.claim: OCR does not scan images in folders excluded by endpoint DLP file-path settings.
claims.quote: If you exclude a path in the endpoint data loss prevention settings, OCR doesn't scan images in those folders.

claims.claim: Endpoint OCR requires network settings that allow blob.core.windows.net endpoints.
claims.quote: For Endpoint Device, ensure that any network settings aren't obstructing the OCR, and a wildcard should be present allowing blob.core.windows.net endpoints.

claims.claim: The Purview OCR file-size maximum for Exchange and Teams is 20 MB.

claims.quote: Image resolution | 50 × 50 px minimum, 16,000 × 16,000 px maximum

claims.claim: OCR extracts only the first two million text characters.
claims.quote: OCR extracts only the first 2 million characters of text.

claims.claim: Exchange OCR scans at most 20 embedded images per file.
claims.quote: For Exchange, the feature supports embedded images in DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, RAR, TAR, ZIP, 7z, and hybrid PDFs (containing searchable text and images) with a limit of 20 embedded images scanned per file.
